payload.name: Preserve explicit ordinal identifiers for creative works
payload.description: When extracting or updating an event memory about a person's creative work or achievement and the conversation explicitly identifies its ordinal position (first, second, third, etc.), include that ordinal descriptor in the memory content.
content: During extraction or CRUD, if a creative work or artifact is explicitly identified by ordinal position (e.g., 'third screenplay', 'second novel', 'first album'), include that ordinal in the event memory content along with the topic or themes.

When the ordinal is confirmed in nearby turns (e.g., 'Is that your third one?' / 'Yep!'), treat it as an attribute of the same work and integrate it into the candidate instead of paraphrasing it away with a generic phrase like 'a personal story'.

solves: During extraction, event memories about a person's creative works or achievements often keep the topic but drop an explicit ordinal identifier (e.g., 'third screenplay') that was confirmed in conversation, so future questions referencing the ordinal cannot be answered from memory. This rule ensures explicit ordinal/sequence descriptors are preserved as durable attributes in the extracted memory.
